prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1385; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of side impact collision at signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a third-party vehicle entering from cross street. Initial scene photos received from insured. Liability appears disputed pending signal timing data. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness; medical attention sought same day. Claimant now represented by counsel; all contact to be routed through attorney's office.

Entry 2: Called claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and request the signed letter of representation and authorization forms. Received confirmation that forms will follow. Requested copies of all treatment records and any prior neck or back complaints. Noted that counsel has asked for a copy of the police report, which has been requested from the reporting agency.

Entry 3: Reviewed police report. Responding officer noted the third-party driver stated the signal was yellow upon entry. Insured stated signal was green. One independent witness listed but not yet reached. Photos show intact rear bumper on the insured vehicle and damage to the driver door and quarter panel. Requested intersection signal logs from the municipality.

Entry 4: Received medical records from claimant's treating provider. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain consistent with whiplash. Physical therapy recommended for six weeks. Treating physician notes claimant reports headaches and reduced range of motion on left rotation. Sent records to independent medical reviewer for causation and reasonableness review. Scheduled follow-up with counsel to discuss status of medical documentation.

Entry 5: Spoke with counsel regarding settlement posture. Counsel submitted a demand package including medical bills, wage loss documentation, and a narrative of injuries. Liability position remains under review pending signal data and witness statement. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect current medical picture. Diary set for follow-up once signal records are received and medical review is complete.
